X.note: The walls are convincing, with peeling plaster, exposed brick and rubble. The figures are stiff, waxy, doll-like clones with hollow or odd heads and ghosted limbs, and they sit pasted onto the scene. The far end of the lane fades into a blank hazy void with no sea, so the depth looks washed out. The Union flag is plausible only loosely, since the 1782 Union Flag (1707–1801) had no Irish saltire, and this one is too small to check.

Y.note: The same excellent wall set gets a better ending: the lane opens onto the sea and a distant ship, so the space has depth and place. The figures are still toy-like, with identical red and blue coats, rigid poses, stick legs and ghost or translucent smears at the left. They are a bit more varied and better grounded than in X, and the rubble and barrels help. The crowd is dense and bunched, and the soldiers' tricorne hats and white cross-belts are roughly right for the period.

why: Same environment, but Y has a believable view of the sea and ship at the end of the lane, and its soldiers are slightly better grounded and more varied, although both still read as game assets.
top_fix_for_weaker: Replace the cloned, ghosted figures with fewer, properly lit and shadowed soldiers in varied poses and clothing, and give the lane end a real sea and rock backdrop instead of a blank haze.
anachronisms_seen: Union Flag details unverifiable at this size (the 1707–1801 flag has no Irish saltire)
uniform colours and cut look generic, with blue coats worn alongside red ones and no clear regiment distinctions
identical clone figures that look like game assets rather than a real garrison
